title: Skill Breakout — Multiplying Decimals & Fractions
topic: Multiplying decimals and fractions as the same function in different notation (bridge to Percent)

items.rationale: 0.4 x 0.6 = 0.24 (4 x 6 = 24, then place the decimal 2 places from the right).

items.prompt: Multiply: 2/3 x 3/4. Give your answer as a fraction in simplest form.
Multiplying decimals and multiplying fractions both represent the same underlying operation because:

choices.A: They always give the same numeric answer no matter the numbers used
choices.B: Both represent multiplying parts of a whole, just written in different notation
choices.C: Fractions cannot actually be multiplied the way decimals can

items.rationale: 0.4 and 2/5 (for example) represent the same value; multiplying either notation represents combining parts of a whole.

items.prompt: A student multiplied 0.3 x 0.2 and got 0.6 by ignoring correct decimal placement. What is the correct product?
items.rationale: 3 x 2 = 6; since both factors have one decimal place each (2 total), the product needs 2 decimal places: 0.06.

items.prompt: A student multiplied 1/2 x 1/3 by adding the numerators and denominators, getting 2/5. What is the correct product, in simplest form?
